title: Answer staff bug reports in Telegram with task status
summary: A developer built a Telegram agent for a client that takes staff bug reports and questions, finds matching issues, and links a plain-language task page with a short report.
agent_role: The agent gathers message context, decides if a message is meant for it, searches issues and system monitoring with read-only access, and returns a readable task link and report; developers built and maintain it.
outcome: Author says such an agent can now be put together in an evening.
what_they_did: A developer's client had non-technical staff who don't speak English and couldn't follow the task board. He connected Telegram to an agent built on the pi-durable framework. The agent collects replies, forwards and attachments, decides if a message is for it, then searches code issues, error logs and the staff CRM. It replies with a link to a plain-language copy of the task and a short report.
how_it_went: The author says the flow can break at almost every step, but the framework handles much of the hard work. He says a proper agent now takes an evening to assemble.
worth_knowing: The hardest parts are gathering context correctly (forwarded messages are still messy) and deciding whether a message is actually meant for the bot.
prompt: Watch [chat group] for staff messages about bugs or questions. For each message, first decide if it is meant for you; ignore it if not. Gather any replies, forwarded messages and attachments as context. Search [issue tracker] for matching issues using read-only access. Reply in [staff language] with a short plain-language summary of the task's status and a link to it. If nothing matches, draft a new issue and show it to me for approval before creating it.

curation.rationale: A real, specific workflow bridging non-technical, non-English-speaking staff to a task tracker via a Telegram agent, with honest notes on failure points; no outcome numbers.
